title: Fractional specialist swaps and auto-trim protocol for cycle resilience
creator: Morgan Reyes
description: Define and validate an operational protocol that allows cycles to borrow fractional specialist time across teams and apply an automated scope-trim (auto-trim) sequence when surge pressure or critical-path delays are detected. The goal is to increase cycle resilience without permanently reallocating headcount: create clear signals, gating rules, a lightweight approval flow, and telemetry for audit and post-mortem analysis.
acceptance_criteria: A telemetry signal definition doc exists that maps surge conditions (blocked critical path, >15% ticket slip risk, >2x unplanned bug hours) to recommended fractional swap sizes
Runbook describing the fractional swap approval flow (who signs off, expected SLAs) is published in Confluence with an example request template
Auto-trim rules implemented as a configurable policy in the cycle-scheduling tool (can be enabled per-project) with unit tests and a feature flag
A pilot across two cross-functional squads executed with before/after metrics for cycle completion, scope slippage, and developer satisfaction
Post-pilot retrospective and proposed changes to cycle planning playbook merged and communicated to PM/Eng/Design leads

decision_log: 2026-01-12 - Decided to use a telemetry-first trigger (observable-driven) rather than manager-request-only to reduce detection latency.
2026-01-25 - Agreed on soft-approval flow: swap requests auto-provision if both source and sink leads acknowledge within 24 hours; otherwise escalate to program manager.
2026-02-03 - Chose to implement auto-trim as recommended scope-priority downgrades (low-risk backlog items) instead of aggressive cancelations to minimize customer impact.
risks: Context-switching overhead could reduce effective throughput of both source and sink teams
Political resistance from team leads if fractional swaps are perceived as permanent resourcing changes
Telemetry false-positives could trigger unnecessary auto-trims; need conservative thresholds and human-in-the-loop overrides
mitigations: Pilot with narrow windows and paired handoff to measure true cost
Require explicit timeboxes for swaps (max 2 weeks by default) and automatic return-to-origin policy
Expose an override in Console for PMs to cancel auto-trim actions within a 48-hour window
pilot_plan: Week 0: Instrument telemetry and create dashboard panels for swap triggers
Week 1-2: Dry-run swap approvals (no reassignments) to validate flows and measure potential throughput loss
Week 3-4: Execute two incremental fractional swaps (0.25 FTE each) and one auto-trim on low-risk scope across two squads
Week 5: Collect metrics, run developer survey, ship retrospective and revised playbook
